feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant public-sector scope. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused metrics beyond platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, reinforcing credibility and growth.  
- Good scope and relevance: combines strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.  
- Strong specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Clarity, Power BI, and concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears across header, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections, especially Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include outcomes such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style consistency issues: mixed punctuation and list formatting in experience entries; inconsistent serial comma use (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs other lists); “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically uneven. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it should be tighter and more differentiated.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning tied to enterprise platforms and communications systems.
- Add 1–2 concrete signals of scale or scope from recent roles to increase impact.
- Trim the long list of functions; emphasize outcomes and leadership breadth instead of repeating skills listed elsewhere.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics, and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads platform strategy, governance, and cross-channel content systems that improve publishing efficiency, audience insight, and digital service delivery, including AI-enabled search and user experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The intro overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader”; avoid restating the same positioning.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/system capabilities would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim softer wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Cross-channel communications leadership”
- Replace generic items with more distinctive strengths: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences”; “Automation and platform integration” instead of “workflow automation and platform integration”
- Consider prioritizing most senior/recent value first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, then communications and multimedia
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Automation and platform integration • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several phrases from the header, especially “enterprise web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled user experiences”
- Overlaps substantially with Topline Skills; keep this section higher-level and avoid tool-specific or near-identical wording elsewhere
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and context.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Built/Developed/Launched…” and trim stacked nouns like “structured content workflows.”
- Clarify specificity where possible: “legislative search,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” “interactive conference display,” “recurring advocacy video series.”
- Consider this cleaner version:  
  **Selected Recent Projects:** AI Hybrid Search — Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Launched a recurring advocacy video series across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI search, microsite work, and advocacy video already appear in Work Experience; keep footer shorter and more portfolio-like.
- “Built/Developed” repetition is manageable, but avoid reusing full responsibility descriptions from experience bullets.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or complexity.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance practices across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.
- Delivered front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing sites, increasing publishing efficiency/reliability.  
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time saved, engagement lift, search success, or adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this role more clearly from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and measurable business impact over channel oversight.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications across web, email, social, and video.”
- Tighten bullets to outcome-first phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, video output, production cost/time savings from the studio, or reporting efficiency gains from the analytics stack.
- Combine lower-value operational bullets: merge governance/publishing standards/cross-department planning into one concise operations-improvement bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version more strategic and less execution-focused.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo roles; frame this here as building institutional capacity, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: operating cadence, editorial coordination, newsletters, and the early advocacy video program.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around building a repeatable channel: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications format.”
- Add outcome/process language where possible: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes and standardized publishing workflows, improving coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid “led digital communications across web, email, social and video” if the Director role already uses nearly identical language.
- “Expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier role and Recent Projects; keep the emphasis here on formalizing the channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo/consulting experience. It should be tightened and differentiated so it signals leadership scope without repeating generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, higher-value language tied to current senior work.
- Emphasize enterprise leadership and governance; de-emphasize generic “content planning.”
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy communications strategy
- If space allows, swap “audience-focused content planning” for “stakeholder-aligned messaging and campaign planning” to sound more senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” already appear almost verbatim in the header/core competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

- WordPress

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability statement, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

- Replace “technical execution” phrasing with more outcome-oriented language such as “platform delivery” or “web platform modernization.”
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier: “enterprise Drupal platforms” or “large public-facing web properties” to connect with the 10,000+ page migration work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JS, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same level of detail here.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies/header language; keep wording distinct.

- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in NACo experience, so this section should summarize rather than repeat.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or add light qualifiers that reinforce seniority and relevance.

Suggested edit
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add concise context instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to sharpen scope: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- If Drupal is the clear flagship, lead with it and consider dropping GitHub Pages if you need space for stronger tools elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places.
- “CMS modernization” already appears in Topline Skills, so don’t add broad capability language here unless you remove it there.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Replace with a tighter list: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value and date the section.
- If space allows, add one brief qualifier tied to impact, e.g. **used for CMS customization, tracking deployment, and workflow automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and shortening the Topline version.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid repeating it in this item unless you specify the technical layer (e.g., GitHub Actions, Workers).

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around orchestration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant systems first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If you have measurable examples elsewhere, align wording to outcomes (e.g., systems used for editorial planning, approvals, cross-team coordination, or process automation), not just tool names.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams/Basecamp may feel low-value if space is tight; prioritize true workflow/automation platforms over general collaboration tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the strategic/operational context you’ve established in recent roles. Make it clearer that these platforms supported enterprise email, member engagement, and campaign communications.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if space is tight; otherwise add light context: **Enterprise email marketing, member engagement and campaign automation using Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic and Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers to strengthen impact: **newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey automation, campaign sends**
- Keep platform names in descending relevance to recent work; if Dynamics 365 is most current, leave first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email bullets; avoid repeating newsletter scale or channel leadership here
- Don’t add generic terms like “email strategy” unless tied to these specific systems

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In a recent-seniority CV, this section should stay lean and tool-focused, with methods framed more precisely.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis**; “SEO” is too broad compared with the tool-based format of the rest of Technical + IT.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI dashboarding** or **executive reporting dashboards** to sound more concrete and senior.
- If space is tight, drop **A/B testing** unless you can support it elsewhere with outcomes; the strongest, most evidenced tools are GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating explanatory language here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content operations, and any concrete outputs or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Tighten the second sentence around execution + supervision: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If possible, split “high-impact digital content” into specific deliverables and outcomes rather than generic phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching/building the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination + launch impact, and trim broad phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the distinctive accomplishment: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast launch the headline result: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or types of stakeholders/program teams served.
- Consider a more active, concise version: “Managed cross-functional innovation/research projects and produced digital content; launched NACo’s first podcast from concept through production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
